about: One section. Jeke-Chelen, coming home from the council that agreed to seize Temüjin the next morning, says so to his wife; she scolds him, and the herdsman Badai, bringing milk, overhears and goes to tell his fellow herdsman Kishiliq. Kishiliq goes to listen and finds Narin-Kegen, Jeke-Chelen's son, telling his own herdsman to tie up two horses for a night ride. The two herdsmen take the horses and ride through the night to Chinggis Qahan to warn him. Several passages are marked in the notes as first readings.
